_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors gold master per the international addendum (Istanbul run — tourism-weighted utilization stack, PREMIUM-substitute pricing per principal override 2026-08-16). Sources: istanbul/REVENUE-INPUTS-ISTANBUL.md + FARE-BENCHMARKS-PREMIUM-ISTANBUL.md (authoritative fare source; supersedes FARE-BENCHMARKS-ISTANBUL.md fare derivations) + CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-ISTANBUL.md + DEMAND-POOLS-ISTANBUL.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-ISTANBUL.md + SPEED-RULES-ISTANBUL.md + NODES-ISTANBUL.md. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals and are UNPRICED on this run (no sourced local rates); the tourism/Islands layer is the headline layer. Berthing and insurance are UNSOURCED in Istanbul this pass — excluded from operating totals and disclosed (fn12 + null row), never guessed. All scenario figures re-verified by script before writing; scenario volumes are authored from the REVENUE-INPUTS bands mirroring the program stack shape (no sourced Istanbul volume plan exists — see _internal.flags_for_jaideep). Demand pools are sourced ridership/visitor/population flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced Istanbul fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders. Committed-seat economics key to the full-speed lines IST-1/IST-2 only; Islands spot seats to IST-2 only; the 10-kn cross-strait shuttle carries no commuter economics anywhere.

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned inside Istanbul's operating premium water market: conventional motoryachts publish roughly 2,700–8,400 lira per hour, speedboat hire runs about $230 per hour, the private sea-taxi hourly rate is about $144, luxury yacht listings reach $455 per hour, and helicopter charter — the market's ceiling — runs €3,000–6,000 per hour.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced ridership, visitor and population flows, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship and overnight cargo — are unpriced until local rates are sourced and are never included in base totals.

fn4.text: All trip times respect the strait's 10-knot over-ground limit and every published harbor rule — set by the Turkish Straits traffic regulation (Presidential Decree No. 1426) and the Istanbul Harbor Master's local marine traffic guide — on a conservative planning basis, with approach and dwell allowances at every call. Open-Marmara segments, where no blanket cap applies, run at service speed. No speed allowance is assumed anywhere in this model.

fn5.text: Seat pricing anchors on Istanbul's existing premium mobility, not the subsidized ferry card: the city's own on-demand sea taxi — a published tariff of 500 lira to open plus 750 per nautical mile, whose shared-ride mode prices a seat at one tenth of the vessel fare — black taxis metered at 1.7 times the yellow tariff, VIP van transfers at roughly $8–16 per person, and the paid business class sold on the region's fast ferries. The blended committed seat weights the corridors with the biggest time win: half long-leg trunk seats, a quarter short-leg, a quarter Islands — corridor bands of about $147–188, $293–377 and $251–314 per seat-month, roughly 40 trips a month at about a third off spot fares. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a Turkey-adapted method: statutory employer burden from the labour ministry's published minimum-wage table, posted coastal wage bands for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), and an explicitly stated 10% allowance line for severance, meals and transport. The model holds the mid benchmark — $23.40 per hour loaded, about $11,400 per vessel-month across 2.5 rosters for a 16-hour day — flat in every scenario; the low benchmark is about $8,200.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded down to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: A conservative thin-fill case — 18 committed seats and 15–45% spot fills — runs modestly below breakeven, about −$2,000 per month. It is disclosed here as the floor of the range; it is not a financing case and is not shown as one.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year with a stated 5% weather-cancellation allowance for southwest-gale days, absorbed in the deliberately thin fills. During Ramadan, midday demand softens and shifts to post-sunset evenings, and the holiday weekend brings an Islands surge — a schedule-shape effect, not an annual-volume one.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the published national commercial electricity tariff with a stated tax uplift — about $0.149 per kWh, or $0.61 per nautical mile. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line roughly doubles; the mid and upside cases remain cash-positive and the conservative floor deepens.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Lira benchmarks convert at 47.76 lira per dollar, the central bank's indicative rate at preparation. Lira fares and tariffs are revised several times a year, so lira equivalents are indicative.

fn12.text: Pier access and hull-and-liability insurance are excluded from operating totals pending sourced Istanbul quotes — they are disclosed as open cost lines rather than guessed. Confirmed quotes will reduce the stated nets.

fn13.text: Road and existing-schedule comparisons are traffic- and season-dependent indications, not measurements. Navier times are computed from route distance at each segment's legal speed with conservative approach and dwell allowances.

copy.headline: Own the fleet behind Istanbul's express water tier.
copy.subline: One vessel, four revenue layers. A tourism-weighted express network on the Marmara shore and the car-free Islands — where full service speed is legal — plus a comfort tier across the strait, earning across the whole day, twelve months a year.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 20 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.
